name: YoungBloodz
notes: Lil Jon's "one finger" rule, authored. The melody is a single high triangle-bell motif of 2–3 notes, so `register` starts at 70 — the highest floor in this batch — `motifPitchCount` is 2–4 and the only percussion lane is a triangle. Everything under it is deliberately emptier than the genre: the kick is fixed at 2 hits with `syncopation` 0.06, the hats are 8ths at the low end of what a hat block is allowed to be, and `emptyBarBias` is 0.28. "Space is the effect" is not a mood note, it is those four numbers. ⛔ `chords.impliedByRiff` is set: the research says the "progression" is one chord plus rests. What replaces progressions is `chordDurationBeats` [3, 16] — the widest here — because the thing that actually varies in this record is *how long the one chord sits*, which is also how the extremely long 808 decay "bleeds across the bar". ⚠ **The bleed itself is not authored and cannot be.** The research's groove is the 808's *release*, and the engine writes note starts and lengths, not envelopes; `bass808.sustain` stays legato and the low register does the rest. Anyone reading this model for the decay will not find it. ⚠ `confidence` is medium: the research sources Lil Jon's minimal-motif method but says the pairing to these specific records — and the 72–82 half-time band, marked [LOW-CONF] — is inference, so `session.bpm` is the least-sourced number here. ⚠ Fill fingerprint for this batch: `gapProb` 0.65 / `descendProb` 0.50 / `rampJitter` 8. ⚠ The bass ceiling came down from 40 to 38 so it stays under a chord part that starts at 39 — `coherence.rs` requires the highest bass note to sit at or below the lowest chord note, and this model overlapped by 2. ⚠ `anticipationProb` raised to 0.15. With `mirror_kick` against a fully locked 808 both parts take every kick, so every bass onset lands exactly on an 808 onset — `coherence.rs` calls that one line played twice rather than two parts locking. The lock is the style and is untouched; the anticipation is what makes them two parts. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 887 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: styles 3, densityRatio 0.5, melody density [1,5]. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 953/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980**, so its style pool was opened: bell_echo, densityRatio 0.55. ⛔ `counter.rs` reads five styles and this roster only ever authored three — `bell_echo` is a real answer shape the engine can already play and the dataset had never asked for. ⚠ `sustain_pad` is deliberately not added: it is a held pad rather than an answer, and adding one to win a variety score would change what the record sounds like. ⚠ **The melody floor was raised from [1,5] to [2,6] because the COUNTERMELODY was saturating at 947/1000 against a floor of 980.** The counter answers inside the lead: a melody allowed to thin to a single note a bar leaves it almost nothing to answer, and no amount of counter styles or density can recover what the lead never played. This is the lead becoming reliably present, not busier — the upper bound is what carries the density and it is unchanged where it was already 6 or more. ⚠ **`melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.28 to 0.1, and this is the parameter that was actually saturating the countermelody** (this model reached 947/1000 against a floor of 980). An empty bar produces an empty counter region, and every empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one — so silence is the one thing a seed cannot vary. Across the roster 57 of the 58 models failing this gate authored an empty-bar bias, averaging 0.246, against 0.115 for the models that passed. The space in the lead is real and is kept; what is removed is the amount of it that made every take collide.
